status.label: Out
status.shortComment: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Friday that Purdy (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game versus the Seahawks, Jennifer Lee Chan of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
status.longComment: Purdy wasn't able to practice during Week 12 prep due to an ankle injury, which will sideline him for the first time this season. In place of Purdy, Mac Jones will earn the spot start Sunday, while the former's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 6, at the Giants. Shanahan added that surgery isn't on the table for Purdy and he's optimistic the QB will be OK to return in Week 13, according to Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com.

status.label: Questionable
status.shortComment: Evans (Achilles) is listed as questionable for Sunday's contest against the Seahawks, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
status.longComment: Evans didn't practice Wednesday before he was listed as limited on Thursday's injury report as he continues to deal with the right Achilles tendinitis that forced him out of a Week 6 matchup with the Commanders. He returned to action this past Sunday versus the Vikings in Mexico City and gathered in six of seven targets for 109 yards and one touchdown on a 43 percent snap share. Evans' status will be clarified about 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff.

status.label: Out
status.shortComment: Watkins (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
status.longComment: Warkins was held out of practice all week due to a groin injury, and the second-year wide receiver will end up missing his third game of the season and first since Week 2 against the Dolphins. Keenan Allen, Jacob Cowing and Demarcus Robinson are all candidates for more offensive snaps Sunday in the absence of Watkins, whose next chance to play is Week 13 against the Giants on Sunday, Dec. 6.

status.label: Injured Reserve
status.shortComment: San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan said Wednesday that Stribling (ankle) is likely at least "a couple weeks away" from returning to practice, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports. "I don't know. I mean, nothing's changed," Shanahan said, regarding a timeline for the rookie receiver.
status.longComment: Stribling was diagnosed with a deltoid sprain of his left ankle after getting injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams in Australia and underwent surgery Sept. 16. The 23-year-old was handed an estimated recovery timeline of about 10 weeks, leaving the 49ers optimistic that he would be ready to play at some point in December. While Shanahan indicated that Stribling's timeline doesn't appear to have changed, the young wideout will need to get back on the practice field before the 49ers can hone in on a more precise target date for him to resume playing. Given the haziness of his return date along with the fact that he could face limitations with his snaps once activated, Stribling likely isn't worth holding in redraft leagues at this point in the season.

status.label: Injured Reserve
status.shortComment: Pleasants (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against Seattle.
status.longComment: Pleasants was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday and ended Week 12 prep with back-to-back full practices. He would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Saturday's NFC West showdown.

status.label: Injured Reserve
status.shortComment: McKivitz (ankle) was placed on the 49ers' injured reserve list Wednesday.
status.longComment: McKivitz was diagnosed with a fractured and dislocated ankle that he sustained in the 49ers' Week 11 win over the Vikings. He's expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season, and Vederian Lowe is expected to take over as the starter at right tackle in McKivitz's absence.

status.label: Questionable
status.shortComment: Greenlaw (neck) is officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game versus the Seahawks.
status.longComment: Greenlaw was limited at practice all week after sitting out the 49ers' contest versus the Vikings with a neck injury, and now his availability for Week 12 seems like a coin-flip proposition. If he is sidelined again Sunday, Garret Wallow could start in his place at linebacker against a run-first Seattle offense.
